notes.title: Happy New Year (2020)!
notes.content:
Hello All,

I just wanted to wish everyone a Happy New Year!  

The sixth anniversary of the game being released on Steam was earlier in December.  And, while I was hoping to have something to release this year, it didn't end up working out.  The Windows 10 compatibility issue that came up a few months back not only impacted It's A Wipe!, which is built on an older version of the Torque game engine, but also the newer version of that engine as well.  With It's A Wipe! I was able to revert back to the DirectX graphics instead of OpenGL to get around the issue, but the newer engine had DirectX completely pulled out of it.  

Long story short, the good news is that someone figured out how to get around the Windows 10 graphics issue with the newer engine.  So, instead of having to abandon the work I had done on a new game and switch over to a completely new engine, I can pick up where I left off.  So, if I can focus up hopefully I'll get a new game out by the end of 2020 :D  

Anyhow, thank you for picking up It's A Wipe and I hope that you have a great new year!

- Harry, Parody Games

notes.title: Windows 10 Compatibility Patch (or, Microsoft Broke OpenGL)
notes.content:
Hello All,

The main build has been switched to Direct 3D forced compatibility mode, as the latest version of Windows 10 (1903) does not seem to be compatible with the OpenGL version used in the game engine.  

For anyone wishing to still use OpenGL on older version, it is still available.  If you go to the game in the Library and bring up the Properties window for it, then go to the Beta section there should now be an "opengl" version (if it doesn't come up, put in the testing code "testing12345".  Effectively, I've made the nonOpenGL executable the new main build.  Please let me know if you run into any issues playing with this change.

notes.title: It's A Patch! (Version 1.9.92)
notes.content:
Happy New Year!

After a complaint that the game was not very playable using 4K monitors, I added an additional screen setting for 3840x2160.  The engine the game was made on, while not strictly predating 4K monitors, was not really made with them in mind - as they were only an extremely high end luxury items at that time.  So, apparently full screen does not work too well with them.

I also added an oversized mouse cursor when in that mode, as apparently the default cursor was tiny.  Now, I don't actually own a 4K monitor so I wasn't able to test this at all.  From what I've heard it's at least playable with this screen setting  ːhappyraiderː

So, here's what's new in 1.9.92:
--------------------------------

* It's Over 4,000! *

- Added a new screen resolution setting that should hopefully make the game playable on a 4K monitor.

--------------------------------

Also, as a reminder, there is currently a player made raid contest going on for the first part of 2018.  You can read the details on the last news announcement or the community forum [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/330620/discussions/0/2549465882914758649/]here[/url].  Thanks for playing!

notes.title: Third Year Anniversary!!! Updates, A Contest, and... well, that's about it really.
notes.content:
Updates???  Updates!?!?

That's right!  To celebrate three years of It's A Wipe! being on Steam I put together a new Player Made Raid for the occasion!  This raid is intended for guilds that have beaten the game and are solidly geared.  Anyone that farmed a ton might find it a little on the easy side, but new guilds will wipe pretty quickly.

Why a Player Made Raid, instead of a new core raid that drops loot, you might ask?  Well, starting today, I want to put forth a challenge to the It's A Wipe! community.  Since I have primarily been working on my next game, Heroes of Kingspoint, I haven't had much free time. I literally put together this new raid yesterday.  Now I do have a lot of experience, since I made the original game and all.  But, I think that, given enough time, you the players can come up with even more entertaining raids.

So, I am announcing the following contest:
From now until April 1st, 2018 any owners of It's A Wipe! may submit a working Player Made Raid to the workshop to enter this contest.  From April 1st until April 30th owners of It's A Wipe! can submit a vote for their favorite raid submitted during the contest period.  The winner will get a beta invite and free copy of Heroes of Kingspoint when it is finally released (probably 2019).  If there are more than 10 submissions, I will also give a 2nd and 3rd prize of a free copy of my next game, just without getting to try it during beta testing.   

I hope that more raids from the community will help everyone get more entertainment out of the game, so this is my attempt to give people a push towards trying their hand at making their own fights.  I know the player made raid system is a little clunky.  So, if you need help getting your raid working or need mechanics added that are not currently available, feel free to either contact me on the forums here or sent an e-mail to support@iawgame.com.

Some small patch notes, relating to player made raid content.  
- Fixed an issue with BombTimer always doing 15 damage.
- Added an Explode command that works like BombTimer, but with a set round instead of the more awkward timer used by respawning bombs.

Thanks for playing the game!
Harry,
Parody Games

notes.title: Happy Thanksgiving, Steam Awards, I'm Not Dead, & Other News
notes.content:
It has been almost a year since I posted any announcements on here, so this is probably well overdue!

First off, Happy Thanksgiving! (At least to anyone celebrating it in the U.S.)

Second thing, I'm still alive and working on the new game I mentioned last annoucement.  If anyone has been keeping track of the blog I mentioned 
( http://kingspointcastle.com/devblog/ ) then you probably already have a decent idea of how it is progressing.  I was hoping to have it ready to try out a Kickstarter next month, coinciding with the third anniversary of It's A Wipe! being on Steam.  But, I think I'm going to push that back until next year.  I don't want to rush it because of some arbitrary deadline.  I want to it playable before trying to get funding for better polish. 

Steam is also doing another round of Steam Awards.  There's a ton of great games out there, but I would appreciate any nods for I.A.W!  Heh, even the somewhat backhanded "Whoa, Dude!".  

No real updates to It's A Wipe! in a while, since as far as I know it is working fine.  I haven't heard about any bugs in over a year, though that might just be due to lack of players ːunhappyraiderː  Just as a reminder, I did put together a utility to be able to make Player Made Raids.  No one has followed up with me for assistance with making one or with a raid to post.  So, I don't know if anyone else has ever used it.  If anyone does have an interest in expanding the game with their own raid ideas, feel free to drop me a line if you find there's any missing functionality in the utility that you need.

That's about all I have to write about at the moment.  Hopefully I'll be back with more news about the new project in a few months.  I hope that everyone has a great week and enjoys the current Steam sale and thank you for taking the time to read this!

notes.title: The Future, Steam Awards, & Feedback
notes.content:
Hello All,

Sorry for the long time between announcements, but for those not reading the forums there was a little discussion about when will something new be coming out for It's A Wipe!?!  The answer is eventually.  I am interested in getting back to doing some more video work, but it is going to take some time to come out with something new with real substance to it.  To that end, I would be interested in hearing people's feedback before I get heavily invested in the next release.

The three basic ideas I'm thinking about are: a sequel to It's A Wipe!, a more serious take on fantasy guild management, or a smaller expansion to It's A Wipe!  Here's my take on the pros and cons of the different options:

It's A Wipe 2! - I'm starting with this, because it is what I'm leaning towards at the time of this posting.  A sequel in my mind would allow for redoing some components of the game to try to improve them, while still keeping the general theme and letting players carry forward their guilds.  I feel like the combat system could use a bit of a revamp to allow for new mechanics and a bit more player interaction.  The cons would be that it would be a decent investment of both time and money to get done.  The original game was done with an intentionally simple design and still took quite a while to complete.  But, there is the original to use as a reference and to build upon.

A Serious Fantasy Guild Management Game - This has most of the same cons as doing a sequel, just with the added disadvantage that there would not really be any continuation of guilds from the original.  However, it would allow for a change in tone that I would not be comfortable doing in a sequel.  This is something that I want to do eventually, even if it is not the next project.

An It's A Wipe! Expansion - The third option would be to do additional content to the existing game.  A big pro to this option is that it would likely take the least time to make.  The real difficulty would be in coming up with novel fights that don't rehash existing mechanics, without really retooling the combat system.  That's why I'm leaning on a sequel rather than additional content for the original.  I did spend a good bit of time adding player made raids as a feature, which has not seemed to see much use from what I can tell.  At least no one's uploaded anything to the Workshop or let me know that anything isn't working with it.

So, let me know your thoughts!  What would you be interested in seeing?  What do people think about Kickstarter funding?  The original was done out of pocket, since I did not want to waste time trying to fund raise when I could be coding.  Though, that might have hurt the art budget.  

I also wanted to mention the Steam Awards that they are doing currently and encourage people to go vote.  It does not have to be for this game, though I would appreciate it.  But, go out there and give indy games some love  :veryhappyraider:

notes.title: It's A Wipe! 1.9.8 1/2 - Mini-Patch!
notes.content:
Hello All,

A few bug fixes have been applied, so I thought that I would roll it up into a nice set of patch notes for anyone that doesn't read the forums :)  Also, one updated button graphic!  Here is what is new in 1.9.8 1/2:

---------------- 

* Unintended Iron Man *
- Fixed (hopefully!) an issue where the new save file index, added in the last patch, was not building correctly for new installs causing saved games to only appear in the session that they were saved in.  If you have this issue, in the %appdata%\Roaming\Independent\IAWGame\game\data folder there should be a saves.txt that you can delete.  The next time you load it will rebuild this index file from the existing saved games.

* Deja Vu *
- Fixed an issue where the first fight of the Insect Temple was also the second fight :/  Some testing code that wasn't removed before posting 1.9.8.

* Free Time! *
- Fixed an issue with Too Much Free Time achievement not triggering.  If you have completed this achievement it will trigger the next time that game is played and the day progresses.

* Shiny New Button *
- The Player Made Raid button has been updated to better match with the rest of the Town Menu.

---------------- 

Please let us know if you do find anything else that you feel may be a bug so we can look into it!  We hope that you enjoy the game!

notes.title: It's A Wipe! - 1.9.5 - One Year Anniversary Patch
notes.content:
Hello All,

Posting this up a little earlier than the actual anniversary, but we wanted to get some of the big changes we've been working on out to everyone.  The biggest item is that this patch introduces a way to make player created raid content and upload it to a Steam Workshop.  It's a little rough around the edges, but we hope to refine it time goes on and we get feedback from users.  There is also a new option when starting a game to have randomized raiders available.

Here's a full list of what is in this patch:

*Even More RNG!*
- When starting a new game you can select Random or Preset (classic style) raiders.  Random will randomize the personalities and availability of raiders.  There is still some modification for difficulty settings.

*Better... or, sometimes much worse*
- When playing with the Random raider selection, new perks and disads have been added.  Disads only appear on Role-Play or harder difficulty settings.

*Not As Easy As It Looks*
- The ability to design player made raids has been introduced.  There is currently 1 demo raid, but we hope that more will be added soon.  A guide has been posted with directions on the community page.

*Faster!*
- The speed on slow, normal, and fast have been increased.  Slow is now the old normal, normal is now the old fast, and fast is about 50% faster.  The fastest game speed remains unchanged.  You may need to change your speed setting the next time you load your game.  If anyone find any graphical glitches on the new fast please let us know.  We ended up disabling a lot of effects on the fastest speed because they didn't display correctly.

*Better Looking Healing*
- Updated the animations for cleric and druid healing.

*TLDR*
- Added some additional tool tip, mainly on the new game screen.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

We're interested in feedback on the new player created content and hope that people will be interested in making some!  If you are working on content and would like some mechanic that is not currently available, please hit us up on the community forums or via e-mail (support@iawgame.com) and we'll see if we can't get it added in a new patch.

We hope that you enjoy these new changes!  And, thank you for playing It's A Wipe!

notes.title: It's A Wipe! Update 1.9.4 - Small Update, but Bigger Changes Coming to Beta
notes.content:
Hello All,

One big change that should hopefully fix an issue some people have had with the game not loading properly.  Apparently the engine would crash out with some graphics cards when doing a check to see if it was Direct 3D compatible.  In this build, it now only checks for D3D compatibility if OpenGL fails or Force Direct 3D has been set.  Other than that, a minor fix for viewing character are and an updated Steam API.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

* Now With Less Crashing *
- Updated executable that no longer does extraneous D3D checks.

* That's Not A Cleric! *
- Fixed an issue in view character art, which was showing the wrong image.

* More Steam *
- Updated to use the latest Steam API.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

In other news, Player Made Content (and a Steam Workshop) should be coming to Beta shortly!

We're looking to target it being put into the Live build next month for the 1 year Steam anniversary.   Right now we've got a system setup to play content, but haven't got an automated builder done yet.  If you want to put in your thoughts on this upcoming feature head on over to the community forums.

notes.content:

*Keyboard shortcuts*
- From the raider selection screen, the 1,2, & 3 keys will now toggle to the corresponding load/save raid configuration option.

notes.title: It's A Wipe! Patch 1.15S!
notes.content:
Hello All!

This patch is mainly to address an issue where certain users with non-English characters in their Windows profile name were unable to save the game.  There are also some minor spelling corrections and a small change in tank setup.

Here are the detailed notes for 1.15S:

- Configurable Save Game Path -

If you experience consistent problems saving the game, you can now configure the save games to a specific path.  You will need to open the local game files and go into the Common directory. Open commonConfig.xml in a text editor and add the line (with the actual directory instead of the XXXX):
<SavePath>xxxx</SavePath>

*Important notes: Do not use a closing slash, and all slashes are forward slashes. For example:  <SavePath>C:/Temp</SavePath> 
Would be a valid entry.

If the game saves for you normally, we don't recommend trying to switch to using a different setting.

- Tanks With No Targets -

In the raid role setup if you have a character assigned as a tank, but give them no targets, they will now switch to be DPS.

- Me No Type Good -

Fixed a few minor typos in item descriptions.

That's it for now!  Happy Holidays!  And, the next update will likely be after Christmas :)

notes.title: It's A Wipe! Patch #3!
notes.content:
Greeting All!

After a few days of debugging we have corrected a number of issues that could cause the game to hang or crash - particularly on a certain fight.  A new way to configure your graphics setting has been made available & one minor buff to gifting made it into this build!

Here's what is new in version 1.14S:

- User Configurable Graphics System Override -

- Since identical physical cards with the same drivers, but different configurations apparently work better with one graphics system than another we are giving users the ability to force the game to try to only use one display option and backed out individual card code.

To change the setting open the local game files and go into the Common directory. Open commonConfig.xml in a text editor and add the line:

<ForceD3D>1</ForceD3D>

(You typically want to try this if you get a black screen on the default settings.)
or,

<ForceOpenGL>1</ForceOpenGL>

(OpenGL is used by default, so you shouldn't typically need to use this one.)

*Note:  Most of the other settings are disabled, sorry no console key, or will cause issues if you change them.

*Note: To prevent your commonConfig.xml settings from getting overwritten if you verify the local cache integrity, you can make a copy called "userConfig.xml" in the same directory and it will use those settings instead.

- Big Bug Fixes -

- The first fight in the Insect Temple should no longer hang on the change to the third phase.

- In uncommon circumstances, healers would get deadlocked trying to decide who to heal next... causing the game to hang while they tried to decide.  A hard cap was placed on how many times they could try to figure it out before it will just skip it and send them on with their existant target list.

- In some timing situations where mobs despawn/respawn combat effects (floaty numbers, etc.) could be trying to draw on a no longer existing object causing an error.  Checks have been added to verify that the target for combat effect still exists (some had checks previously, but now everything should.)

- In some timing situations an end of turn check would carry over into the end of turn phase causing minor internal errors (I don't think this would directly crash the game, just throw out of range exceptions).  Checks have been added to skip checking if the turn has ended if the fight is already over and you are getting loot.  

- Improved Gifts -

- All, but the top level, of gifts have had some benefits added.  Raiders now consider them loot.  While you won't see an immediate improvement to morale, it should boost some behind the scenes numbers for raiders who have gotten passed over on items in raids.

That's it for now!  If people are no longer seeing crash issues (*fingers crossed*) we'll be moving on to reviewing some less critical issues.  A number of quality of life improvements have been suggested that we would like to add, some wonky agro needs to be reviewed, and a few item description typos have been pointed out ;)  Hopefully we'll have another patch of just improvements, at least for testing, by the end of this weekend.  

I hope everyone continues to enjoy the game and we'll keep trying to improve it! ːhappyraiderː

notes.title: It's A Wipe! Day 4 Patch Notes
notes.content:
Hello All!

We are continuing to try to address issues that have been found following the Steam release.  This patch contains a few definite fixes for some specific issues, as well as additional debugging output to help try to investigate problems that we cannot reproduce locally.

Here is what is new in build 1.13S:

Graphics Handling Improvements:

- We have added in conditional direct 3D graphics support.  If you experience an issue where you just get a black screen when trying to launch the game, please try to use the Video testing beta build.

To load this build, go to the game in your library and bring up the properties window. From there go to the Beta tab. It will allow you to select a Video Testing release from the drop down. If you download that build (and possibly verify the local files) it will force direct 3D graphics instead of the default OpenGL.  If this does work to resolve the issue, please send our support staff a copy of the console.log found in the local game files for It's A Wipe! so that we can add your video card to the list to use direct 3D in the core build.

In this build we have added direct 3D support for:
GeForce GTX 780 Ti
AMD Radeon HD 5800 Series
AMD Radeon HD 6900 Series

Fixed:

- The Delete Saved Game functionality has been corrected.  It was not working in the initial Steam build.

Debugging:

- Additional output to the console log has been added for set out of range errors and save game creation errors.

Tweaks:

- In trying to track down an issue that can cause the game to hang on some fights, we did a pass through the mob actions.  Some loops were cleaned up, which might help with this issue.  I would be pleasantly surprised if this did fix the issue entirely, but that's what the debugging additions are for!

Informational:

- The "Testing" build is no longer set to force direct 3D.  If you are having black screen issues, please make sure to use the "Video Testing" version.

- The user that has been in touch with us about being unable to save at all appears to have invalid characters in his windows user profile name.  The save games get created under the <drive>:\users\<logged in user>\ folder on Windows  7 & 8 machines.  Removing nonstandard characters from the profile should address the inability to save.  Though, we may look at adding an option to configure a save game directory in a future update.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

If other issues come up please let us know and we will look into them.  We hope that people are enjoying the game, and we will continue to work to improve the stability as best we can!

notes.title: It's A Wipe! Day 2 Patch
notes.content:
Hello All!

Thanks to everyone who has supported the Steam release of It's A Wipe!  We have put together a number of fixes based on issues reported by the community after release.  

Here's what has changed in version 1.12:

Fixed:

-  Corrected an issue with Tank Switch where it would skip the last mob, which was a major issue with solo boss fights.  It should now loop on the enemy list correctly!

- Ludicrous speed is now less crazy.  All crash issues reported seem to have been caused by timing problems with the highest speed setting.  Fast is about twice as fast as normal, where ludicrous was about 50% faster than that.  It has been reduced to 40% faster and some checks have been added to try to prevent problems when timing events would run into one another.

Tweaks:

- Cleaned up some of the auto-selection during Raid Role Selection, so that it more consistently selects the first player when appropriate.

- After the first turn, Stick With The Plan is highlighted as a default option on successive turns.

- Increased the Tank Switch agro bonus when a new tank initially tries to get main threat on a target.

- Made minor code clean ups to the save game path handling.

- Updated some of the graphics handling of the core engine.

New:

- This is only half done, since new art tends to take longer than coding, but a new option to enable/disable vertical sync has been added to the Video Options.  This can be toggled using the V key on the Video options screen, but should only need to be changed if you are seeing a frame rate issue.

Important Notes:

- Some AMD HD series cards have problem with OpenGL, which is the graphics utilized by out engine.  Users may experience a black screen when trying to launch.  This has been an issue with other games made on this engine, and some notes about trying to backdate the drivers can be found here: 
http://www.spacepiratesandzombies.com/forums/viewtopic.php?f=15&t=1659	
 and elsewhere on the internet.

We'll see what we can do on our side, but it may take a bit to add other graphics handling options.

- A couple users have reported issues saving the game the very first time the game is launched.  If you experience this, try closing and restarting the game.  From what we have heard, saving has worked consistently after this.  We tried making some changes with this patch, but can't say definitively that they will correct this issue.

Thanks to everyone who has supported our game on Steam!  We hope that you enjoy the game and we'll continue working to try to make playing a smoother experience. ːveryhappyraiderː
